solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time in lesson certain to expire

indicators.note: in places the time letter inside the word for lesson

parts.note: the lesson of a fable is its moral

explanation.surface: A teacher's clock-watching remark that a dull lesson is bound to run out of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal being is one destined to die, so certain to expire is a fair paraphrase.

clue.text: Short new style altered in decorous fashion

parts.note: mod is a clipped form of modern, meaning new

indicators.note: altered signals that the letters of style are changed in order

explanation.surface: A brief new fashion has been toned down to look more proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting modestly means behaving with propriety and restraint, which is a decorous manner.

clue.text: Save most of cake in small room

indicators.note: in places the shortened cake inside the room abbreviation

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for room

indicators.note: most of means the cake's word loses its last letter

parts.note: an eclair is a cream-filled cake

explanation.surface: Rescuing the bulk of a cake left in a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to recover or rescue it, which is what save means here.

clue.text: Education reforms offered lots to people

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of education are formed anew

explanation.surface: Changes to schooling gave people many opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' reads as plenty, but it means items for sale at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Items put up at an auction are lots, offered to bidders for the highest price.

clue.text: Goes round without penny, being this?

definitions.text: Goes round without penny, being this?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the turned word sits outside the penny
round tells us the word for goes is turned back to front

parts.note: goes, as in leaves, means departs

explanation.surface: Someone wandering about with no money in their pocket, and the question of what that makes them.
explanation.walkthrough: DEPARTS read backwards gives STRAPED; 'without' (outside) puts that round P for penny. The whole clue then describes the answer: someone without a penny is short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped, often 'strapped for cash', is informal for being short of money, which is what having no penny means.

clue.text: Sorting out bothers — role for such a person

definitions.text: Sorting out bothers — role for such a person

indicators.note: sorting means the letters of the following words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing the job of someone whose work is fixing other people's problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes 'out bothers' and 'role' together; read whole, the clue also describes the person's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is someone employed to find and fix faults or resolve disputes.

clue.text: Suitable garment for kitchen sink stage part

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a protective garment worn when washing up
second meaning: the part of a stage in front of the curtain

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink suggests kitchen-sink drama, linking the two halves, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment tied over clothes while cooking, and the forward section of a theatre stage beyond the proscenium arch.

clue.text: Contributing to epic as someone who produced most expensive pictures?

indicators.note: Contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a grand film about an artist whose works fetch huge sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings by the Spanish artist have sold for record sums at auction, among the priciest ever.

clue.text: Weapon hoisted on end of gantry liable to drop off

indicators.note: on places the reversed weapon on top of the final letter in the down entry
hoisted, in a down clue, means the word for weapon is written upwards

parts.note: a sword is a weapon

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of gantry

explanation.surface: A weapon raised onto a crane might fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop off' reads as falling from the gantry, but it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drowsy is sleepy and likely to nod off at any moment.

clue.text: Manufacturing arrangement for channel, one connected to Internet

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a duct is a channel or pipe
I is the Roman numeral one
online means connected to the internet

explanation.surface: A setup for a TV channel with someone hooked up to the web.
explanation.definitionFit: A production line is a factory system where items pass through successive stages of assembly.

clue.text: Stuff carried on board badly cracked before journey

indicators.note: before places the shuffled letters ahead of the word for journey
badly signals that the letters of cracked are put together wrongly

parts.note: to journey is to go

explanation.surface: Cargo damaged in transit arrives badly cracked after its trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck cargo is freight stowed on a ship's open deck rather than in the hold, so it is goods carried on board.

clue.text: Clergyman hasn't finished page — that's right

indicators.note: hasn't finished means the clergyman's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar has left his sermon notes incomplete, and someone confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, as opposed to the verso on the left.

clue.text: Abridged book is read after editing? Penguin, for example

indicators.note: after editing says the letters given are rearranged, as an editor reorders text

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book, a cut-down form of the word

explanation.surface: A shortened volume revised for the publisher Penguin Books.
explanation.walkthrough: Penguin looks like the publisher, which suits the talk of books and editing, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A penguin is a flightless bird of the southern oceans, so it is one example of a bird living by the sea.

clue.text: Burdens added to bishop, hence lots of extra pay

indicators.note: added to joins the word for burdens onto the bishop's letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
onuses are burdens or responsibilities

explanation.surface: A bishop given more duties gets rewarded with extra pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonuses are payments made on top of normal wages, so several of them are extra pay.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory type of pale colour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dud, something or someone that disappoints
second meaning: a pale yellow shade

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase describing a washed-out person, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty car or a failure is called a lemon, and the same word names the light yellow of the fruit.

clue.text: Making certain changes, with nothing added

indicators.note: changes says the letters of certain, together with the zero letter, are moved about

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone making sure of alterations, with nothing extra put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of bringing something into being, which is what making means as a noun.

clue.text: Drunken painter, say, in highly dangerous position

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a painter is a rope for tying up a boat, an example of a rope

explanation.surface: A tipsy artist finds himself in a precarious spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Painter is not an artist but a boat's mooring line.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope is a wire stretched high up for acrobats, so being on one is a perilous situation.

clue.text: Manoeuvred to get position Scot contemplated

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
to eye something is to look at or contemplate it

explanation.surface: A Scotsman eyeing up a good spot after some manoeuvring.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey for position is to scheme or manoeuvre to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Something between rounds eaten in golf club

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a snack of filling between two rounds (slices) of bread
second meaning: ... in Kent is home to Royal St George's, a famous golf club

explanation.walkthrough: Rounds suggests rounds of golf, but here a round is a slice of bread. Sandwich is a town in Kent whose Royal St George's links hosts the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack with filling held between slices of bread, and also the Kent town famous for its championship golf links.

clue.text: Firm including a worker in commercial transaction, initially

indicators.note: in places the article and the worker inside the other letters

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, AD

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of transaction

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a hired hand

explanation.surface: A company taking on a worker during a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but it is the adjective meaning unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant refuses to be persuaded, holding a firm, unyielding position.

clue.text: How belligerent American operates gadget

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, a fighting American; with 's it gives GI'S
how someone operates is their modus operandi, MO; the word operates completes the phrase

explanation.surface: A question about how a combative American gets things done.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as GI'S MO: the soldier's way of working.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, also spelt gizmo, is a gadget or device whose name one has forgotten.

clue.text: Note no longer as expression of love

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a pound or dollar, recalling the old one-pound note

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as though love is no longer written down, but the clue holds two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smacker is slang both for a pound or dollar and for a loud, smacking kiss.

clue.text: Deeply understand female, in short

indicators.note: short means the phrase for in loses its last letter

parts.note: someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: Getting to know a woman thoroughly, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' means at home, and 'short' clips it to AT HOM; two little clue words supply most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, like sounding the sea's depth, so to grasp it thoroughly.

clue.text: A gang running to desert

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A gang of criminals hurrying off to the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' reads as the sandy noun, but it is the verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to leave them in the lurch, which is to desert them.

clue.text: Act on desire to be top person in field

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the word for act above the word for desire

parts.note: to do is to act
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Following one's ambition to become the leader of one's profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or senior member of a group or profession.

clue.text: Excel militarily? Not in offensive

parts.note: someone not in is out
rank means foul or offensive, as of a smell

explanation.surface: A commander declining to join a military offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' suggests a military attack, fitting the surface, but it means foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrank is to hold a higher rank than someone, the military way of being superior.

clue.text: What's said to get attention about a volume that's serious

indicators.note: about means the attention-getting call goes round the other letters

parts.note: hey is a call to catch someone's attention

explanation.surface: Someone calling out about a book that turns out to be weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy can mean grave or weighty, as in a heavy conversation, which is serious.

clue.text: Unusually choice opener for sport

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of choice appear in an unusual order

parts.note: a key opens a lock, so it is an opener

explanation.surface: An odd choice of first event for a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' suggests a first match, but it is a thing that opens a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice hockey is a team game played on ice with sticks and a puck.

clue.text: E.g. Christian seen in strange retinue after mass

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters following the mass letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of retinue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchgoer spotted among an odd entourage after Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian is not a believer here: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian led the Bounty uprising, so he is the classic example of a sailor who rebelled.

clue.text: Become furious in office of bishop and cardinal, say

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or jurisdiction
cardinal is a shade of red, named after cardinals' robes

explanation.surface: A bishop and a cardinal losing their tempers in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal looks like a churchman to go with the bishop, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for losing one's temper suddenly and becoming very angry.
